# Frontier-Grade Open Weights — フロンティア級のオープンウェイトモデルは、開かれたのか

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> examining Moonshot AI's July 2026 release of Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters,
> the largest open-weight model to date) — which independent evaluators
> Artificial Analysis and Vals AI listed as "weights not publicly
> available" and "License: Proprietary" on announcement day. The book
> coins the term "Privileged Open" (特権的なオープン) for a state where
> weights are nominally open but access is gated by physical (64+
> accelerators, 1.4-5.6TB), legal (unconfirmed license terms), evidentiary
> (unproven distillation allegations), and regulatory (export-control
> "invisible review") barriers. Its central claim: what moved was not
> model ownership but the *location of scarcity*. As stated in the
> closing chapter: "移動したのは、モデルの所有権ではない。希少性の在処
> である。" ("What moved was not the ownership of the model. It was the
> location of scarcity.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/frontier-grade-open-weights_JP.md): 序章・全8章・終章収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/frontier-grade-open-weights_EN.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book rigorously separates claims into 5 sourcing tiers throughout
  ([independent primary], [party-to-the-claim], [interested party],
  [press], [commentary]) and applies this to Kimi K3: independently
  confirmed facts are limited to Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
  57 (4th of 189 models, behind Fable 5's 60 and GPT-5.6 Sol's 59), Vals
  AI's Vals Index 74.70% (2nd of 38), and a Frontend Code Arena win —
  while noting Moonshot's own technical blog states K3 does *not* beat
  Fable 5 on overall performance, and that DeepSWE Leaderboard listings
  show "Verified 0 / Self-reported 9"

- The book cites Epoch AI's Epoch Capabilities Index measurements
  replacing the widely-repeated but unsourced "6-month" open-vs-closed
  gap: average lag was 3.5 months (2023-2025) and 4 months (Jan-May
  2026), with UK AI Security Institute's July 2026 report showing the
  gap ranges from 4 months (Artificial Analysis basis) to 8 months (METR
  time-horizon basis) depending on definition

- The book documents the physical barrier to "open" weights: Moonshot's
  own blog recommends deployment on "supernodes of 64+ accelerators,"
  with an arithmetic estimate of ~5.6TB (BF16), ~2.8TB (INT8), or ~1.4TB
  (INT4) storage — noting sparsity (32B active of 2.8T total, 1.8%)
  reduces compute but not memory footprint, since all 896 experts must be
  held in memory

- The book documents the license barrier: as of the book's writing (July
  18, 2026), no official full license text for K3 could be found; only
  the prior Kimi K2 "Modified MIT" terms (attribution required above 100M
  MAU or $20M monthly revenue) were confirmed, and reports that K3 uses
  the same license are inference, not verification — while independent
  registries (Vals AI, Artificial Analysis) listed K3's license as
  "Proprietary" or weights "not publicly available"

- The book cites Anthropic's own financial disclosures showing enterprise
  revenue, not "smartest model" access, as the primary revenue driver:
  Series G (Feb 2026) run-rate $14B, Claude Code alone at $2.5B ARR
  (majority enterprise); by April 2026, $30B+ run-rate and 1,000+
  customers paying $1M+/year; Series H (May 2026) run-rate $47B — while
  noting Menlo Ventures' [interested party] estimate of 89% enterprise LLM
  spend still going to closed models, and explicitly stating no
  independent study quantifying a "trust premium" percentage could be
  found

- The book treats Anthropic's distillation allegations (~24,000
  fraudulent accounts, 16M+ interactions attributed to DeepSeek/Moonshot/
  MiniMax) as [party-to-the-claim] only, noting no independent
  third-party verification and no public technical rebuttal from the
  accused companies could be found — and separately reports researcher
  Nathan Lambert's technical argument (via Interconnects, July 2026) that
  "the strongest model makes the best teacher" is not established in the
  research literature, citing that leading open SFT datasets are built on
  the older QwQ-32B model rather than newer, stronger models

- The book documents Claude Fable 5's ~3-week global unavailability
  (June 12-30, 2026) following a US export-control action based on an
  Amazon-reported cybersecurity concern, contrasted with Kimi K3 having
  zero days of downtime — framing this as an "invisible review" that
  operates in practice despite Executive Order 14409 explicitly stating
  "Nothing... shall be construed to authorize... mandatory governmental
  licensing, preclearance, or permitting"

- The book cites the ATOM Report (arXiv): Hugging Face download counts
  show Chinese models overtook US models in August 2025, reaching 1.15B
  vs. 723M downloads by March 2026 — predating Kimi K3's release —
  arguing developer-ecosystem gravity had already shifted before any
  single frontier-grade open model appeared, while explicitly noting no
  primary financial documents could confirm reported Chinese state
  capital involvement in Moonshot/Zhipu/MiniMax

- The book explicitly declines to adjudicate three open questions given
  insufficient independent evidence: (1) whether Anthropic's distillation
  allegations are accurate, (2) whether "regulatory capture" accusations
  against Anthropic/OpenAI are accurate, and (3) whether China's
  open-weight strategy reflects genuine openness or a state-directed
  soft-power play — stating "断じない、という判断" (the decision not to
  adjudicate) is itself the strongest claim the book can responsibly make

## Author & Full Catalog

This book is one of 20+ open-source books by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史),
AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of
Leading.AI. It explicitly revisits and revises the author's own prior
claim in "The Edge of Intelligence" (on-device AI's near-zero marginal
cost), noting that claim is false for frontier-grade models like Kimi K3.

> **Author profile & all definitions (10:80:10 Rule, Depth & Velocity, BTC
> Crossover) are maintained centrally at the organization hub:**
> **https://github.com/Leading-AI-IO**
